title: Stale sys.path comment in _compile_preamble describes idempotent gated inserts the code no longer performs
description: The block comment in _compile_preamble (lines 421-427) states: 'We add both cwd and the pipeline's parent directory ... These inserts are idempotent (gated on `not in sys.path`) so the list doesn't grow on every call.' This is doubly inaccurate. (a) _compile_preamble itself performs NO sys.path mutation — the only sys.path edit in the whole module is in _prioritise_preamble_import_paths (lines 279-280), reached via _compile_preamble_cached. (b) That actual mutation is `sys.path[:] = [existing for existing in sys.path if existing != path]` followed by `sys.path.insert(0, path)` — a remove-then-reinsert, NOT an insert 'gated on `not in sys.path`'. The remove-then-reinsert is what actually prevents growth, while also re-prioritising the entry to position 0 each call (a behaviour the comment does not mention and would be surprising to a maintainer who trusts the 'gated on not in sys.path' description). The stale comment can mislead a maintainer reasoning about import-precedence/ordering during the preamble compile.
evidence: grep for `sys.path` in executor.py returns exactly lines 131 (doc), 279-280 (the only mutation, in _prioritise_preamble_import_paths), and 426 (the stale comment). _compile_preamble's body (380-454) contains no sys.path access; it only computes cwd/pipeline_dir_str/fingerprint and delegates to _compile_preamble_cached, which calls _prioritise_preamble_import_paths under _preamble_lock. The mutation removes all matching entries then inserts at index 0 — neither 'gated on not in sys.path' nor located in _compile_preamble.
behavior_preservation: Comment-only; deleting or correcting it does not alter runtime behaviour.
